To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the defective presentation by tumor-infiltration dendritic cells is independent of the presence of Treg, and that the defective antigen presenting function of the tumor-draining dendritic cells cannot be overcome by the depletion of Treg.
the defective presentation by tumor-infiltrationg dendritic cells of tumor antigens is not due to CD4+CD 25+ regulatory T cells.
tumor-infiltrating DC are defective in their antigen presenting function, and this defect is not due to CD4+CD4+25+ Treg.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of CD4+ regulatory T cells in tumor immunity.
the role of dendritic cells in tumor immunity.
the role of regulatory T cells in tumor immunity and the development of novel strategies to enhance antitumor immunity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the defective presentation in B16.Ova tumors is not due to Treg.
the tumor micro-environment is a major factor in the defective presentation of tumor antigen in vivo.
“tumor-infiltrating DCs are defective in Ag presentation regardless of the presence of CD4+ CD25+ Tregs”.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tumor microenvironment is not the sole factor responsible for the failure of dendritic cells to stimulate naïve antigen-specific T cells in vivo.
the defective presentation by dendritic cells is not due to regulatory T cells, but to a more general defect in antigen presentation by the tumor microenvironment.
the defective antigen presentation by dendritic cells in the tumor microenvironment is not due to regulatory T cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

tumor-infiltrating and tumor-draining dendritic cells from mice bearing established B16 melanoma are defective at presenting tumor-derived antigens in vivo, regardless of the presence of CD4+ regulatory T cells.
tumor-infiltrating DCs are defective in their antigen presentation function regardless of the presence of CD4+ CD25+ regulatory T cells.
dendritic cells in the tumor-drained lymph node do not seem to play a role in the induction of tumor-specific immunity.
